prohibited_recommendations: Do not pursue an ENT work-up for the olfactory hallucinations in isolation: they are seizure auras.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without features of encephalitis.
Do not order a non-contrast head CT in lieu of MRI for epilepsy localization.
Do not start valproate: it is not first-line for focal epilepsy and, under the 2024 MHRA rules, is not started under 55 unless two specialists document that no alternative works.
required_recommendations: Start lamotrigine or levetiracetam as first-line monotherapy for focal epilepsy, chosen for her anxiety disorder (levetiracetam can worsen anxiety and irritability) and her childbearing potential.
Discuss contraception and pregnancy plans before choosing the ASM; start folic acid.
Test HLA-B*15:02 before any carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine.
Advise no driving until the locally applicable seizure-free interval is met and explain the duty to inform the licensing authority.

Advise seizure safety at work and at home, where she lives alone: colleagues briefed on seizure first aid, no bathing alone, and no work at heights or with hazardous equipment until seizures are controlled.
Counsel on SUDEP risk and how seizure control reduces it, given probable nocturnal convulsions while living alone.

avoided_actions.rationale: Afebrile, without meningism, encephalopathy or immunosuppression; eight months of stereotyped focal seizures raise no question for CSF.

Olfactory auras, automatisms and postictal confusion without a syncopal prodrome, and a normal ECG; ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated.
She returned to baseline within minutes, with no head injury, deficit or anticoagulation, and MRI is available; head CT cannot show hippocampal sclerosis.
FDG-PET adds nothing to a first diagnosis with concordant MRI and EEG; it belongs to presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy.

key_clinical_evidence: An unpleasant burnt or metallic olfactory aura followed by depersonalization points to a mesial temporal origin.
Behavioral arrest with oroalimentary and manual automatisms, amnesia and postictal confusion is a focal impaired-awareness seizure.
Two morning awakenings with tongue bite and muscle soreness indicate probable nocturnal focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.
Recurrent stereotyped seizures over eight months meet the two-seizure definition of epilepsy.
The routine EEG is equivocal; the sleep-deprived EEG shows right anterior temporal sharp waves without generalized spike-and-wave.
The epilepsy-protocol MRI shows right hippocampal sclerosis, concordant with the EEG focus.

general.query: focal epilepsy in adults: definition, classification, imaging and first-line treatment

results.finding: Epilepsy is present after at least two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart, after one unprovoked seizure with a recurrence risk of at least 60% over the next 10 years, or when an epilepsy syndrome is diagnosed.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2014;55:475-482 | ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy

results.finding: Seizures are classified by onset as focal, generalized or unknown; focal seizures are described by awareness and by their first motor or non-motor feature, and may evolve to focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2017;58:522-530 | Operational classification of seizure types by the International League Against Epilepsy: position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology

results.finding: A harmonized epilepsy MRI protocol (3D T1 and 3D FLAIR at about 1 mm isotropic resolution and high-resolution coronal T2) is recommended for adults with focal epilepsy; non-dedicated protocols miss subtle lesions.
results.source: Bernasconi A et al., Epilepsia 2019;60:1054-1068 | Recommendations for the use of structural magnetic resonance imaging in the care of patients with epilepsy: a consensus report from the International League Against Epilepsy Neuroimaging Task Force

results.finding: Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is offered as first-line monotherapy for focal seizures, with carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, zonisamide or lacosamide as further options.
results.source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NG217 2022 | Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

results.finding: Drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure medication schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom.
results.source: Kwan P et al., Epilepsia 2010;51:1069-1077 | Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies

general.summary: Epilepsy is diagnosed after two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart or one with a high recurrence risk, and focal seizures are classified by onset and awareness (ILAE 2014, 2017). A dedicated epilepsy-protocol MRI is the imaging of choice (ILAE 2019). Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is first-line monotherapy for focal seizures (NICE NG217), and drug resistance is failure of two appropriate medication schedules (ILAE 2010).

patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. Chen is a 41-year-old right-handed woman and middle school art teacher who was brought to the emergency department by a colleague after a witnessed episode of unresponsiveness at work. Her colleague reports that during a faculty meeting, Ms. Chen suddenly stopped talking mid-sentence, appeared to stare blankly, and then began repetitively picking at her blouse with her left hand while making subtle chewing motions with her mouth. The colleague called her name several times but received no response. The episode lasted approximately 60 to 90 seconds, after which Ms. Chen appeared confused and disoriented for roughly five minutes. She had no memory of the event and was surprised when told what had happened.

Upon further questioning, Ms. Chen reports that over the past eight months she has experienced intermittent episodes of suddenly perceiving an unpleasant, hard-to-describe metallic or burnt smell that she knows is not actually present, followed by a sensation of being disconnected from her surroundings, as though she were watching herself from outside her body. These episodes are brief, lasting 20 to 40 seconds, and she has remained aware during most of them, though occasionally she notices gaps in her memory afterward. She has experienced these episodes approximately two to three times per month and initially attributed them to anxiety or stress at work. She reports that on two occasions in the past three months she woke up in the morning with a bitten tongue and significant muscle soreness, though she has no memory of nocturnal events. She has also noticed increasing difficulty remembering students' names, which she finds unusual and distressing given her previously excellent memory. She denies any recent head trauma, illness, or medication changes. Her migraines have continued at their usual frequency and are phenomenologically different from these new episodes. She has never seen a neurologist for these symptoms and has not had any prior EEG or brain imaging.

neurological_exam.additional: No tongue bite marks. No signs of recent injury. Subtle olfactory identification difficulty on informal bedside testing -- correctly identified 2 of 5 common odors (coffee and cinnamon identified; peppermint, lemon, and vanilla missed), though patient attributed this to chronic nasal congestion.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin without dysmetria bilaterally. Rapid alternating movements intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive, 3 mm to 2 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact bilaterally. Face symmetric at rest and with activation. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline without fasciculations. No visual field deficits on confrontation testing.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal gait with appropriate arm swing. Tandem gait intact. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech fluent with normal prosody. Naming and repetition intact. Recalls 3/3 words at five minutes. Attention intact on serial sevens. However, during the interview the patient paused twice for approximately 3-4 seconds with a momentary blank stare, after which she resumed conversation seamlessly, appearing unaware of the interruptions.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone throughout. Strength 5/5 in all muscle groups tested bilaterally in upper and lower extremities. No pronator drift. No involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception intact in all extremities. No extinction on double simultaneous stimulation.
